checks.name: regression-suite
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --lib --test engine --test attachment --test calibration --test physics --test behavior_contract

checks.name: performance-controls
checks.command: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --example engine_cost && cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path truelearner/Cargo.toml -p truelearner-body --example link_cost

findings: Each changed meeting now classifies its participant chain once and carries boundary and completed-path information in MomentChange.
Inert boundary and ordinary drive moments bypass react_into and leave ReactionScratch untouched; learning-bearing and ambiguous moments retain the full reaction path.
ReactionView separates immutable arena, link-memory, and live-return borrows from mutable activity scratch, so the whole ReactionScratch is no longer moved or replaced.
Fresh release samples no longer contain react_into or ReactionScratch drop glue on the primitive or ordinary-link common paths.
The old black-box contract passed 3 of 3 tests, the compact-body contract passed 6 of 6 tests, and checkpoint passed 9 of 9 tests.
The known advanced body-law boundary remained exactly 17 passing and 11 failing tests, with no regression among previously passing laws.
The independent primitive-wave median was 22.35 ns versus 40.01 ns before this change, and active propagation was 23.91 ns per link versus 35.17 ns.
residual_uncertainty: The relevance predicate deliberately over-approximates uncertain boundary structure, so some ultimately empty structured moments may still enter reaction construction; learning-heavy reaction cost is unchanged and is not represented by these two common-path benchmarks.
